First, we write $F(s)$ as a sum of partial fractions, as follows: 

$$
\frac{2}{{s}^{2}-1}=\frac{2}{(s-1)(s+1)}=\frac{1}{s-1}-\frac{1}{s+1}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{t}} & =\frac{1}{s-1},\,s>1 \\ L{{e}^{-t}} & =\frac{1}{s+1},\,s>-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the addition property of the Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-1}-\frac{1}{s+1}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-1}}-{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+1}} \\  & ={e}^{t}-{e}^{-t}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{2}{{s}^{2}-1}$ is $f(t)={e}^{t}-{e}^{-t}.$
